title: Mutational constraints on RSV F and its neutralization by antibodies.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and parsed with pandas: all_antibodies.csv (9,824 rows x 20 cols, 0 duplicates on site/wildtype/mutant, 504 sites 26-529, 14 antibody escape columns + cell entry + region); func_effects.csv (10,260 rows, incl. 154 stop codons and 504 wildtype-synonymous controls); all 6 per-selection func_effects files, from which I computed the cell-entry replicate ceiling (mean pairwise Pearson r = 0.839; 0.896 within-library, 0.801 between-library); Nirsevimab-IgG/Fab and Clesrovimab-IgG mut_effect.csv with their 4 per-replicate columns, giving escape replicate r = 0.05-0.24 per mutation (0.16-0.51 at site level); Nirsevimab-IgG_mut_icXX.csv (10,208 rows, explicit 'log2 fold change IC50' column); protein.fasta (504-residue F sequence); natural-variation tables (RSV-A 234 rows, RSV-B 220 rows); the Lassa GPC partner file 293T_filtered_func_effects.csv (9,610 rows, byte-identical 7-column schema). Verified positive control in the files: mean effect of stop codons -2.872 vs missense -2.024 vs wildtype-synonymous 0.000. Verified the cell-entry/escape confound: Spearman +0.38 to +0.52 over all mutations, falling to +0.06 to +0.22 among functional mutations only (n=3,258). Confirmed Zenodo record 21049420 (MIT licence) and that the paper's data availability statement names exactly the file I downloaded.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That the assay is lentiviral pseudovirus deep mutational scanning in 293T-TIM1 cells at biosafety level 2; the biophysical bivalent-IgG-buffering model; the specific newly identified escape sites (67, 73, 206-207, 210-211, 215-216); that natural sequences came from Pathoplexus; and that resistant strains are currently rare. Europe PMC full text returned HTTP 500 and the supplementaryFiles endpoint returned a non-zip, so Supplementary File 1 was not retrieved - but the data availability statement says it duplicates all_antibodies.csv, which I did open. Column semantics (that 'effect' is a log2 enrichment relative to wildtype) come from the dms-vep-pipeline-3 documentation, not from a units string inside the CSV.

a1_downloadable.note: No login, no application. Fetched 15+ CSVs directly from raw.githubusercontent.com; Zenodo record 21049420 archives the whole repo (327 MB zip) under an MIT licence. Verified by downloading.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Labels are literally columns: 'cell entry' and 14 named escape columns ('Nirsevimab-IgG escape', etc.) in one 9,824-row table, plus 'effect' in func_effects.csv. Nothing to construct. Verified in the files.

a3_inputs_present.note: site/wildtype/mutant plus the complete 504-residue F protein sequence in results/gene_sequence/protein.fasta. No accession resolution needed. Verified both.

a4_units_stated.note: Consistent log2 scale throughout; the icXX files name units explicitly in the header ('log2 fold change IC50 mean'). 'effect' units (log2 enrichment vs wildtype) come from pipeline docs, not from the CSV itself.

a5_enough_rows.note: 9,824 mutations in all_antibodies.csv, 10,260 in func_effects.csv, 103,552 rows in long format across 14 antibody/format combinations. Counted in the files.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~12 MB downloaded; largest single file 4.2 MB
a6_fits_laptop.note: Every file under 1.5 MB except two summaries. One 504-residue protein, so ESM-2 masked-marginal scoring is a single forward pass. Verified by file sizes.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Paper's data availability statement points at results/summaries/all_antibodies.csv; it holds 504 sites x ~19.5 mutants = 9,824 rows, matching 'nearly all mutations'. 'cell entry' matches func_effects 'effect' (both max 1.598). Verified.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels trace to barcode sequencing counts from pseudovirus selections - a physical measurement, with raw counts included in the repo. Values are fitted by a global-epistasis/polyclonal estimator, but the protein sequence never enters that fit, so no circularity and no feature-derived leakage. Verified by inspecting the per-selection count-derived files.

existing_models.name: ESM-2 (a protein language model from Meta, open weights, used zero-shot via masked-marginal scoring)
existing_models.score_and_split: No RSV F number exists. On ProteinGym (a benchmark of 250+ deep mutational scanning assays, 2.7M variants) it is a standard zero-shot baseline; ProteinGym's own report notes GEMME wins on viral proteins and that only 28 of the assays are viral (8 influenza A, 6 HIV, 4 phage, 2 SARS-CoV-2), none RSV.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: ProteinGym's maintainers name low-MSA-depth and viral proteins as where sequence-only models are weakest, and multimodal sequence+structure models as what now wins.

existing_models.name: StabilityArc (2026 preprint, supervised cross-protein variant-effect model built on ESMC-600M embeddings)
existing_models.score_and_split: 0.7134 Spearman correlation under 66 strict leave-one-protein-out evaluations over 134,794 ProteinGym variants, versus 0.6526 for the strongest zero-shot baseline ProSST-2048. This is the honest split our project would also use.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: They argue the held-out-protein setting forces a purely biophysical landscape rather than memorised mutational pathways; generalising to protein families unlike the training set remains the open part.

existing_models.name: EVEscape (Nature 2023, Marks lab; combines an EVE generative sequence model with structural accessibility and residue chemistry to score antibody escape)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported as comparable to high-throughput experimental scans at anticipating SARS-CoV-2 pandemic variation using only pre-2020 sequences, and extended to influenza, HIV, Lassa and Nipah. No RSV F evaluation retrieved.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Their own figures state EVEscape and experiments make distinct, complementary escape predictions - i.e. agreement with measured escape is partial.

existing_models.name: Molecular modelling of RSV F escape (Journal of Virology 2022; molecular dynamics plus FoldX free-energy changes for motavizumab binding)
existing_models.score_and_split: Predicted >6-fold binding-affinity changes for specific mutations (N63T, I64V, D200E, K201N) validated case-by-case in vitro. No genome-wide split, no correlation against a full mutational scan - it predates this dataset.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: They note some antibody-resistant mutants require two simultaneous residue changes, which single-mutant modelling cannot anticipate.

existing_models.name: Cross-protein transfer (CPT) models for disease variant prediction (open, trained on deep mutational scanning from only five proteins)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported state-of-the-art clinical variant interpretation for unseen human proteins; evaluated on clinical annotations, not on viral entry-protein cell-entry assays.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Transfer from a handful of training proteins to distant unseen families is the stated frontier.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (esm2_t33_650M_UR50D, a protein language model with open weights; the 150M checkpoint as a faster alternative)
backbone.hardware: Laptop CPU, 16 GB RAM. The protein is one 504-residue sequence, so masked-marginal scoring yields zero-shot scores for all 9,824 mutants from a single forward pass; frozen per-position embeddings cache once in well under a gigabyte.
backbone.licence: MIT for ESM-2; MIT for the RSV data repository (confirmed on Zenodo record 21049420). Both permissive, commercial use allowed.

integration.partner_dataset: The ~12 companion dms-vep pseudovirus cell-entry scans from the same lab and pipeline (Lassa Josiah GPC verified: 9,610 rows, identical 7-column schema; plus Nipah F, Nipah RBP, rabies G, chikungunya E, influenza H3/H5/H7 hemagglutinin, SARS-CoV-2 spike variants, 229E spike, HIV Env BF520/TRO11), with PDB 5UDC and 6OUS prefusion/postfusion F structures for solvent accessibility, and Pathoplexus natural RSV sequences for observed mutation frequencies.
integration.join_key: (protein, site, wildtype, mutant) across dms-vep repositories; PDB residue number for structure features; the 'sequential_site' column for reconciling numbering with natural reference strains.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does a model trained on how mutations break cell entry across a dozen different viral entry proteins measured by one identical assay predict the mutational tolerance of a newly scanned virus it has never seen, and does the natural variation actually circulating in RSV respect that measured fitness landscape?

controls.positive_control: Verified in the files: the 154 stop-codon mutations average -2.872 on the cell-entry scale versus -2.024 for missense and exactly 0.000 for the 504 wildtype-synonymous rows, so any working model must rank stops as the most damaging. Second control: the literature-known nirsevimab escape mutations K68Q/N and N201S/T must appear in the top few percent of the escape ranking.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle the cell-entry labels and confirm collapse to the per-site-mean dummy; replace ESM-2 features with same-shaped random noise; ablate feature blocks (position only, amino-acid identity only, embeddings only); shuffle within site to confirm the grouped cross-validation is really grouping.
controls.external_validation: The Lassa GPC cell-entry table I already downloaded (9,610 rows, identical schema) and the other ~12 dms-vep proteins, for leave-one-protein-out testing. Plus the two natural-variation tables in this repo (RSV-A 234 rows, RSV-B 220 rows) which carry observed mutation counts, and the companion Journal of Virology 2025 study of RSV F evolution against human sera.

honest_claim_h3: Among mutations to the subtype A Long-strain RSV F protein that were sampled in a two-library lentiviral pseudovirus assay in 293T-TIM1 cells, the model ranks how much each mutation reduces cell entry, with accuracy bounded by a replicate ceiling of r=0.839 that I measured from the six independent selections; it does not claim to predict the replicative fitness of real RSV, nor per-mutation antibody escape, whose labels replicate at only r=0.05-0.24 and are therefore only meaningful aggregated to the residue position.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a protein's amino acid sequence to predict how much each possible mutation breaks the virus's ability to enter cells.
plain_idea.train_on: Each example is one amino acid substitution in the RSV (respiratory syncytial virus) fusion protein - the position, the original residue, the new residue, and the surrounding sequence context. I counted 10,260 such measured mutations covering 504 of the protein's positions, and a further ~9,610 for Lassa virus in an identical table for transfer experiments.
plain_idea.predict: The output is a number for how much that mutation reduces the virus's cell entry. The true answer comes from a laboratory experiment: harmless virus-like particles carrying mutated versions of the protein are mixed together, allowed one attempt at infecting cells, and DNA barcodes are counted before and after to see which mutants survived. Averaged over six independent repeats.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Groups monitoring resistance to nirsevimab and clesrovimab - the two antibodies now given to infants to prevent severe RSV - must decide which newly sequenced virus strains deserve expensive laboratory testing, and a validated predictor would make that triage possible from sequence alone. Even if the model fails, we learn how reliable these increasingly popular escape-mapping experiments actually are.

more_or_better_data.why: RSV F appears in none of ProteinGym's 250+ assays, which contain only 28 viral assays (8 influenza A, 6 HIV, 4 phage, 2 SARS-CoV-2). This adds 10,260 measured mutations on a class I viral fusion protein, a structurally distinct family those models have never been tested on, plus ~12 companion scans using one identical assay rather than ProteinGym's heterogeneous mix.

confidence_score.why: I verified 6 independent selections for cell entry and 4 per antibody, plus effect_std, times_seen and n_models columns in every file. That lets us attach a measured per-mutation reliability to each prediction. ESM-2, GEMME and EVEscape report no calibrated per-variant uncertainty, and ProteinGym mostly does not expose replicate-level data.

models_beatable.why: The RSV-specific escape predictor (molecular dynamics plus FoldX, Journal of Virology 2022, closed, validated only mutation-by-mutation) is clearly beatable. ESM-2 zero-shot is a soft target. But ProSST-2048 (0.6526) and StabilityArc (0.7134) are 2025-2026 models already evaluated under strict leave-one-protein-out, which is the honest split, so the headroom on the generic fitness task is modest.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Two conditions fail. The companion dms-vep proteins do measure the same quantity with the same assay and pipeline, and ESM-2 zero-shot can be run as our baseline - but our supervised model does not see a strict superset of what the zero-shot model sees, and transfer across viruses with different receptors and different fusion mechanisms can easily add noise rather than signal. Escape and cell entry are also different labels, so no new data guarantees better escape prediction.

label_elsewhere.sources: ProteinGym (250+ deep mutational scanning assays, retrieved its paper and benchmark pages), MaveDB (known resource for the same label type), and the ~12 companion dms-vep viral entry protein scans - I downloaded the Lassa Josiah GPC table and confirmed it has the identical 7 columns and 9,610 rows.
label_elsewhere.join_key: UniProt accession plus residue position for ProteinGym/MaveDB; (protein, site, wildtype, mutant) for the dms-vep family.
label_elsewhere.why: Mutation-effect labels of this exact kind already exist for millions of variants across 200+ protein families, which gives both a far larger training corpus than this one paper and a ready-made held-out-protein test to check whether a model learned biophysics or just memorised RSV F.

risks: Mutations at the same residue position behave alike, so a random split over the 9,824 rows puts siblings of each test mutation in training and a per-site average alone would look good; the 'site' column (504 values, ~19.5 mutations each) is present so this is avoidable.

Antibody escape values correlate with the cell-entry effect at Spearman +0.38 to +0.52 across all mutations (I measured this), so a model could score well on escape merely by predicting fitness, which protein language models already do well; the correlation drops to +0.06 to +0.22 once restricted to the 3,258 functional mutations.

Per-mutation escape labels sit near the noise floor (replicate r = 0.05-0.24), so any impressive escape number is more likely leakage or a bug than signal; evaluating on the top 1% of escape by consensus mean is itself biased - I measured replicate correlation going negative there (-0.26 to -0.06), a winner's-curse artifact.

Library batch effect: between-library replicate agreement (r=0.801) is measurably worse than within-library (r=0.896), so library A versus B identity is a batch factor correlated with the measurement.

ESM-2 was pretrained on UniRef, which contains RSV F and every partner protein, so a 'held-out protein' is unseen only to the trained head, never to the backbone - the transfer claim must be worded accordingly.
leakage_plan.split: Primary: group by the 'site' column, holding out whole residue positions (504 groups), with a stricter variant grouping by the 'region' column (7 antigenic-region values). Both columns were seen directly in all_antibodies.csv. For the transfer claim: leave-one-protein-out across dms-vep repositories, where protein identity is the repository and the schema match was verified against Lassa GPC.
checks: Shuffle cell-entry labels and confirm performance collapses to the per-site-mean dummy, not to zero.
Train a model using the cell-entry effect as the only feature to predict escape, and report that as the confound floor any escape model must clear.
Filter to functional mutations (cell entry > -1, n=3,258 verified) before making any escape claim, and compare every escape number against the replicate ceiling I measured rather than against zero.
Report nearest-neighbour sequence and positional similarity between each held-out site and the training sites, and ablate ESM-2 features against position-only and amino-acid-identity-only models.
leakage_plan.verdict: Manageable for the cell-entry label, because the grouping columns exist and the noise ceiling is known; a serious risk for antibody escape, where the label is near its own noise floor and is confounded with fitness.

success_criteria.metric: Spearman rank correlation between predicted and measured cell-entry effect on held-out residue positions, because the decision a surveillance team makes is a ranking - which mutations in a newly sequenced strain are tolerated enough to matter - not an absolute value.
success_criteria.baselines: Trivial: per-site mean of the other mutations at that position, and a single-feature substitution-matrix/hydrophobicity model - both computable from the columns I verified, values not yet measured. Non-trained: ESM-2 masked-marginal zero-shot, obtainable in one forward pass. Published anchors on the same leave-one-protein-out style split: StabilityArc 0.7134 and ProSST-2048 0.6526 Spearman over 66 ProteinGym proteins.
success_criteria.success: Spearman >= 0.60 on held-out residue positions for cell entry while beating ESM-2 zero-shot by >= 0.05, and recovering the literature-known nirsevimab escape mutations K68Q/N and N201S/T within the top 2% of the escape ranking.
success_criteria.kill: If after one week a frozen-ESM-2-plus-head model cannot beat the per-site-mean dummy by >= 0.05 Spearman on held-out sites for cell entry, stop. Separately, if no filtering raises per-mutation escape replicate agreement above r = 0.3, abandon escape regression entirely and report only the site-level result and the measured noise ceiling.

ambitious.why: It publishes biology-first machine learning with a public-health hook, which this would be if cross-virus transfer clearly works and the model independently recovers the known nirsevimab escape sites, making it usable for real RSV sequence surveillance.

realistic.why: It publishes exactly this kind of benchmark-and-evaluation contribution: a harmonized multi-virus entry-protein mutational-scanning benchmark with honest held-out-site and held-out-protein splits, a measured replicate noise ceiling, and modest but real gains over ESM-2 zero-shot.

fallback.why: It publishes methodological negative results and data resources, so even the bare finding that per-mutation antibody-escape labels replicate at only r=0.05-0.24 - meaning escape must be evaluated at residue-position resolution - plus the harmonized table, would stand on its own.

pitch.headline: Nearly every mutation in the RSV fusion protein, measured for cell entry and for escape from seven antibodies including nirsevimab, in one 9,824-row table.
pitch.what_makes_the_data_unusual: I opened the files: 10,260 mutations over 504 positions, zero duplicates, six independent selections giving a measured replicate ceiling of r=0.839 for cell entry. Absent from ProteinGym's 250 assays. MIT licence, 12 MB total.
pitch.the_win: Spearman 0.60 or better on held-out residue positions for cell entry, beating ESM-2 zero-shot by 0.05, while independently recovering known nirsevimab escape mutations K68Q/N and N201S/T in the top 2%.
pitch.even_if_it_fails: We publish a measured noise ceiling: per-mutation antibody-escape labels replicate at only r=0.05-0.24, so escape is learnable at residue-position resolution and not per mutation. That reframes how every escape-mapping experiment should be evaluated.
pitch.who_wants_it: The Bloom lab (dms-vep), the Marks lab (EVEscape), and the nirsevimab and clesrovimab resistance-surveillance groups, who must decide which newly sequenced circulating RSV strains justify expensive laboratory neutralization testing.

ml_idea: Two linked tasks on one 12 MB table. (1) Core: freeze ESM-2, a protein language model with open weights, and fit a small head to predict the measured cell-entry effect of each of 10,260 amino acid substitutions in the RSV fusion protein, evaluated by holding out whole residue positions (504 groups) and whole antigenic regions (7 groups), with the measured replicate ceiling of r=0.839 as the target to approach rather than exceed. Add structure features (relative solvent accessibility and distance to the antibody epitope) from PDB 5UDC and 6OUS. (2) Transfer: pool the ~12 companion dms-vep cell-entry scans, which use one identical assay and pipeline (Lassa GPC verified as 9,610 rows with byte-identical columns), and ask under leave-one-protein-out whether a model trained on other viral entry proteins predicts a virus it has never seen - a question that is informative whichever way it resolves. Antibody escape is treated as a secondary, site-level-only target, because I measured its per-mutation replicate agreement at r=0.05-0.24, which rules out honest per-mutation regression and is itself the project's guaranteed publishable finding.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed, from file sizes I measured directly (every file under 5 MB, ~12 MB downloaded in total) and from the fact that the target is a single 504-residue sequence: masked-marginal scoring gives zero-shot values for all 9,824 mutants in one forward pass, and frozen per-position embeddings for a handful of proteins cache in well under a gigabyte. The pandas profiling I actually ran took seconds.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Already done in this evaluation, and it should be anyone's first step: compute pairwise replicate correlation across the six per-selection func_effects files (0.839 - cell entry is well measured and the project is alive) and across the four per-antibody replicate columns (0.05-0.24 - per-mutation escape regression is dead on arrival). Running it costs one script and settles which of the two labels the project can be built on.

verdict_reason: All eight Part A killers pass, verified by opening the files rather than reading the paper: labels are already columns in a single clean 9,824-row table, the 504-residue input sequence ships with the data, there are zero duplicates, the licence is MIT, and the paper's data availability statement points at exactly the file I downloaded. The whole working set is 12 MB and the backbone step is one forward pass, so this is a genuine laptop project with a 3-hour path to a feature table. The decisive verification is that I measured both noise ceilings: cell entry replicates at r=0.839 across six independent selections and is a solid regression target, while per-mutation antibody escape replicates at only r=0.05-0.24 and must be aggregated to residue positions. That single finding both protects the project from its main failure mode and is a publishable result on its own, which is why the project cannot produce a useless answer. The field is real but not closed - ESM-2, GEMME, ProSST, StabilityArc and EVEscape are open and honestly evaluated, yet none has touched RSV F, which is absent from ProteinGym's 250 assays and belongs to a class I viral fusion protein family those models were never tested on. The ~12 companion dms-vep scans, sharing one identical assay and a schema I confirmed against Lassa GPC, turn this into a leave-one-protein-out transfer question rather than a crowded leaderboard chase. The honest limits are that everything comes from one lab, one cell type and one subtype A strain, and that the label people actually care about for surveillance is the noisy one.
